body.statement: Characterize \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{G}(H,\Omega)\) by a finite-dimensional primal--dual program, determine a least-favorable distribution over donor faces, and construct an attaining confidence kernel for arbitrary fixed \(J\), arbitrary positive definite \(\Omega\), and multiple-zero-label faces. Determine exactly when the optimized rule strictly improves on \(C_n^{\mathrm{proj}}(\alpha)\) after passage to the Gaussian experiment.
body.justification: This is the paper's central open content: an exact honest-diameter frontier on the stratified donor-face experiment.
body.gap: Restricted-Gaussian confidence-set duality does not cover a target map that changes with the active zero-coordinate face, and post-selection methods do not optimize worst-face expected diameter.
body.consumer: A solution yields the shortest defensible ATT interval for every fixed donor menu and supplies a reusable decision primitive for tie and moment-selection problems.
